findings.source: Tomkinson GR et al. (iGRIPS Group). International norms for adult handgrip strength: a systematic review of data on 2.4 million adults aged 20 to 100+ years from 69 countries and regions. J Sport Health Sci 2025;14:101014 (online 2024-12-06).

findings.peak: Peak at 30-39 y: 49.7 kg men, 29.7 kg women (published abstract; a preprint said 47.8 kg men)

Other rows taken from secondary sites (joingetfitapp.com, fitnessnorms.com) that cite iGRIPS; P5/P50/P95 agree across those two sites, P20/P80 seen only on joingetfitapp. International pool includes lower-strength regions, so slightly below US/UK/N-European values.

recommended.measure: Max grip of the stronger hand (best single squeeze, either hand), kg, adults ~20-39 (peak); Jamar-type dynamometer, seated, elbow 90 deg
recommended.derivation: Unweighted mean of the iGRIPS (Tomkinson 2025) DIRECT P5/P20/P50/P80/P95 values for the four 5-year bands 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39 (bands differ by <2 kg, so averaging percentiles approximates the pooled percentile closely but is not identical to it). No normal-distribution assumption. Cross-checks: Dodds 2014 UK peak median 51/31 kg (normal-model derived 5-95: men 35-67, women 21-41); NHANES dominant-hand mean 50.3 kg men 30-34; PURE Europe/N.America men <40 median 50 kg (IQR 43-56); Leyk 2007 young German men mean 55 kg, women 33.5 kg. Western populations sit ~1-3 kg above iGRIPS at P50.

recommended_all_ages_note: No source found giving a single pooled 18-80 percentile table per sex. iGRIPS/NHANES/Canada give only age-banded tables; pooling would require population weighting not available from snippets. Suggest age-adjusting instead (iGRIPS male P50 ~48.8 kg at 40-44; JOSPT male dominant medians ~45.9 kg 40-44, 44.8 kg 50-54, 40.3 kg 60-64, 36.3 kg 70-74).
assessment: iGRIPS (2.4M adults, protocol-harmonized, direct P5-P95 incl. P20/P80) is the best single source for exactly the requested percentiles. Main caveats: (1) several iGRIPS rows came via secondary sites citing the paper, though they match the one row seen in the paper itself; (2) international pool slightly underestimates Western gym-going users (UK/US medians ~50-51 kg men, ~31 kg women); (3) device matters - cheap digital spring dynamometers can read differently from Jamar; (4) do NOT mix with NHANES 'combined grip' (sum of both hands, ~2x). 'Elite' at P95 (~65 kg men / 40 kg women) is population-elite, not athlete-elite: trained strength athletes commonly read 60-80 kg (men) and ~45 kg (elite women), with top grip specialists far higher (unverified 100+ kg claims).
